rows.notes: The study is a systematic literature review (SLR) of 38 primary studies on drone-based plant disease detection; it reports no own experiment, survey, measurements or model runs. Its results are counts of disease types, drone types, stakeholders, ML tasks, image types, algorithms, crops and challenges across the reviewed papers. It makes no own finding that UAV/AI systems improve disease diagnostics, optimize treatment strategies or support targeted agrochemical application; such benefits are only mentioned in the introduction citing other work. Q1 is 'no', so Q2-Q9 are 'no'. Not a precondition/upstream case since the study is not primary; the subject (drone disease detection) does match the claim's technology.
